topics.name: Whole numbers up to 1 000 000
misconceptions: Learners think a number with more digits is always bigger, or mix up the places when writing a number in expanded form.

topics.name: Adding and subtracting larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners line up digits wrongly in columns, or forget to carry and borrow when moving between places.

topics.name: Multiplying and dividing whole numbers
misconceptions: Learners think multiplication always makes numbers bigger and division always makes them smaller, or forget what a remainder is.

topics.name: Multiples and factors
misconceptions: Learners confuse multiples with factors, or think 1 is not a factor of every number.

topics.name: Reading time and working out duration
misconceptions: Learners confuse the hour and minute hands, or think 100 minutes make one hour.

topics.name: Common fractions
misconceptions: Learners think a larger bottom number means a larger fraction, or read the top and bottom numbers as separate whole numbers.

topics.name: Equivalent fractions
misconceptions: Learners change only the top number to make fractions equal, or forget to multiply or divide both top and bottom by the same number.

topics.name: Perimeter and area
misconceptions: Learners add all the sides to find area, or confuse perimeter with area.

topics.name: Perimeter and area of compound shapes
misconceptions: Learners include inner lines when measuring the outside edge, or count the middle squares twice when finding area.

check.reason: Perimeter and area is taught again in Term 3 at a deeper level; it may be one repeating topic or a new one.
options: Keep as a separate topic building on Term 2
Merge into one topic spanning Terms 2 and 3

topics.name: Decimal fractions
misconceptions: Learners think 0,5 is smaller than 0,25 because 25 looks bigger than 5, or line up the decimal comma wrongly.

topics.name: Two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects
misconceptions: Learners think a square is not a kind of rectangle, or miss the hidden faces, edges and corners when counting.

topics.name: Capacity and mass
misconceptions: Learners think a taller container always holds more, or mix up grams and kilograms when changing units.

topics.name: Number patterns and number sentences
misconceptions: Learners guess the next number without testing the rule, or think the missing number has to be at the end of the sentence.

topics.name: Money and simple budgets
misconceptions: Learners forget to change between rands and cents correctly, or think change is always a whole rand amount.

topics.name: Data handling
misconceptions: Learners think the tallest bar means the most important choice, or misread the scale on the graph axes.

topics.name: Position and movement
misconceptions: Learners mix up left and right from someone else's point of view, or think north means up on every map.

leftOut.name: Percentages
leftOut.reason: The plan says percentages is a Grade 7 topic and is not taught in Grade 5.
